cells.tense: Right now a clear seeing is arriving and you are holding it steady.
cells.act: let the mind find its own limit in the thing
cells.ask: Take something you're trying to understand and follow it until thought reaches its own edge. Stop there. That edge is the clarity; you don't have to move past it.
cells.core: A new way of seeing is arriving in you, and it's still whole — nothing has been decided by it yet. That's not confusion. It's the first cut of clarity before it cuts. You can hold it without forcing it to mean something about what has to end, and let something end without dressing it up as revelation. When this is working, the people near you feel seen rather than filed. The clearing you're in asks for endings, and your gift is that clarity comes before the verdict. Let it finish arriving before you aim it. What needs to end will tell you when it's ready to be named. Until then, seeing is enough work for one week.
cells.sheetLine: See it first. Name the ending after.
cells.verb: Letting a clear seeing land before it cuts
cells.place: The clearing where what was has to end

cells.tense: Soon you'll be seeing clearly and you'll want to clear everything at once.
cells.act: bring the possibility all the way into form
cells.ask: You've begun something. Close it in the form it actually has before you decide what else goes.
cells.core: The clarity is coming, and it's coming faster than the endings can move. So it races ahead and starts clearing spaces nobody has left yet. You'll notice it as a pressure to have it all sorted by a deadline you didn't choose. What saves you here is smaller than a vision: finish what you already began. Not the next ending — the current one. What was only possible, standing finished, with the door closed instead of slammed. That's how clear seeing becomes something you live in rather than something you act out on the people near you. Let one form complete itself, and the rest will show their timing instead of you dictating it.

cells.tense: You have been standing at this doorway long after it closed behind you.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: There's something unfinished that keeps waiting on you. Pick it up once more and carry it through to the end.
cells.core: The clarity has become a place you stand rather than a thing you use: you can see the shape of what ended, and you keep living beside it instead of past it. That's not stupidity. It's a door you already walked through, still being treated like a decision you haven't made. You don't need to feel clear before you finish something. Choose one unfinished task, give it one honest hour, and then step away from it. Clear seeing doesn't come first; it comes as a by-product of completing something. One hour, this week, and then you stop. That's the whole ask.
cells.sheetLine: Finish one task and the door is behind you.

cells.tense: You are already clearing things without noticing that you are the one doing it.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: At some point today, notice something that has just arrived — in the conversation, in you, in the quiet — before you decide what it means or what it replaces.
cells.core: The clearing is happening through you, and your story is that it's happening to you. Situations end near you, and it reads as natural. You're not wrong about the endings; you're wrong about who's doing them. What's arriving right now is smaller than a turning point and more useful than one: a new tone in someone's voice, a sentence you didn't plan, a quiet after something ended. Notice one of those while it's still new, before you decide what it is. You don't need to choose every ending. You do need to see that the choosing has been yours. Nothing else changes today except that. The moment is fresh whether or not you claim it.
